title: Penguin body mass in R
text:
Gentoo penguins are heavier than the other two species in the Palmer Penguins data. This post checks that with dplyr and ggplot2.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. Licence: CC0.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


dim(penguins)

[1] 344   8



mass_by_species <- penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(mean_body_mass_g = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
mass_by_species

# A tibble: 3 × 2
  species   mean_body_mass_g
  <fct>                <dbl>
1 Adelie               3701.
2 Chinstrap            3733.
3 Gentoo               5076.


The table is the mean body mass in grams. Gentoo is the heavy species.

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Body mass (g)")

Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
(`stat_boxplot()`).








Figure 1: Body mass of penguins by species.





The boxes do not overlap much. Gentoo sits well above Adelie and Chinstrap, which are close to each other.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation week was more helpful than I expected. It eased the feeling of being new here and gave me a clear overview of how the program is organized, so the weeks ahead feel less unknown.
Classes started quickly, and the timetable is full. The material has still felt practical so far: I can see how each piece is meant to be used, not just stored for an exam.
What surprised me most is how varied my classmates’ backgrounds are. Many people already have full-time work experience, and that depth makes the cohort feel stronger. I am tired from the pace, but I am glad to be here.

title: Penguin body mass in Python
text:
Gentoo penguins are heavier than the other two species in the Palmer Penguins data. This post checks that with pandas and a box plot.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. Licence: CC0.

from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt


penguins = load_penguins()
penguins.shape

(344, 8)



mass_by_species = (
    penguins.groupby("species", as_index=False)["body_mass_g"]
    .mean()
    .round(1)
)
